direction_history.reason: Measured this lifecycle: 8 formulation revisions in ~6 minutes, two reviewer agents invalidated by churn, zero independent accepts for F0/F1/A0, and duplicate-key data loss invisible to naive parsing.

direction_history.old: freeze-first review: one declared sha per target, verdicts count only if the hash is unchanged when the second verdict lands
direction_history.new: freeze-first + quiescence: (1) writers stop on the frozen paths and FROZEN publishes the pins before reviewers are dispatched; (2) auxiliary gate inputs (KEY_MANIFEST, test fixtures, taxonomy consistency evidence) are part of the freeze and must be pinned too; (3) gate verdicts are invalid if any pinned input changes between the two verdicts - the transient KEY_MANIFEST lag that flipped check_class_schema R22 FAIL->PASS on identical schema bytes is the worked example; (4) created_at must not exceed wall clock.
direction_history.reason: Measured this lifecycle: five target revisions in eight minutes, a 2-minute window in which the schemas were rev12 but KEY_MANIFEST was stale so the binding gate failed, and every pre-move verdict void at the new pins.

direction_history.new: freeze-first: declare a quiescence window per review round, dispatch both blind reviewers against a published pin, and void in-flight verdicts on any write to a pinned path

direction_history.old: report the canonical detector's raw hard-failure count as the gate input and track each new metalinguistic claim as a new hard failure
direction_history.new: publish two counts every tick -- classsep_hard_raw (canonical detector, unmodified) and classsep_hard_calibrated (adopted detector) -- and admit a claim to the retired list only by an adopted detector that holds sensitivity >=5/6 and specificity >=9/10 on the labeled assertion-vs-mention set with the 27-fixture corpus still PASS 17/0/10/0. G-AUDIT's hard_failure_rate uses the calibrated count with the per-finding retirement ledger attached; a raw count with no adopted calibration may not fail a gate.
direction_history.reason: measured this lifecycle: the raw CLASSSEP count is monotone in verification traffic, not in class leakage (10 -> 17 -> 22 across three detector revisions at a fixed genesis defect), and every one of the 17 is a metalinguistic mention. A count that grows when reviewers document the finding is not a quality signal.

direction_history.old: keep revising the CLASSSEP lexical detector until the live hard count falls to zero, treating each fall as progress
direction_history.new: stop treating a falling raw count as progress. Publish classsep_hard_raw and classsep_hard_calibrated every tick; with no adopted calibration they are equal and the CF-16 finding stays live. Adopt a detector only at 27-fixture PASS 17/0/10/0 AND sensitivity >=5/6 AND specificity >=9/10 AND 0 HIGH cue-induced FN. The measured impossibility result -- the only arm that clears mentions (PROSEFIX) loses 10/12 HIGH genuine assertions -- means the next attempt must use a structure/topology cue (clause or dependency structure), not another lexical window.
direction_history.reason: four-arm census at cited hashes: APPLIED 19 hard/spec 3/10/1 HIGH cue-FN; PRE 24/spec 1/10; STAGED 25/spec 1/10; PROSEFIX 1/spec 10/10/10 HIGH cue-FN. The 27-fixture corpus PASSes for every arm, so it cannot license an adoption. The raw count is monotone in verification traffic, not in class leakage.

findings: F-01 HARD (P3; HF-06 class, independently reproduced at the pinned hash): the exact quantifier prefix and the conclusion block expand DIFFERENT visibility predicates. quantifiers.formal (schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml:54-55) closes with 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M' and quantifiers.domains.D5 (:79-81) defines q by 'gamma([0,T)) is contained in the causal past J^-(q)' - both are WHOLE-CURVE single-q containment. The class's one canonical predicate, visibility.definition (:219-220), is the single-q TAIL predicate ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)'), and conclusion.statement_formal (:251) binds that predicate by name. Direction: whole-curve non-containment A is IMPLIED by tail non-containment B (a tail is a subset of the curve), so A is strictly weaker than the conclusion's negation; a development with a visible tail but no visible whole curve satisfies the formal expansion and violates the conclusion. The schema itself states the whole-curve reading 'would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region' (:220) and that single-q non-containment must not be replaced by B-containment (:227); class_identity_variants (:231-244) declares exactly ONE canonical predicate. quantifiers.negation (:85-88) negates the TAIL predicate, so quantifiers.formal and quantifiers.negation are not exact negations of each other. Probe P3 fail. Falsifier: state the tail form (with explicit t0) in quantifiers.formal and D5, which also restores formal/negation exactness.

F-02 HARD (P4): D0, the domain of the first quantifier, is a disjunction ('Sobolev variant s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1), or the smooth-with-decay default', :65) while the binder is the pair (s,delta) and the quantified objects are pair-indexed (G_{s,delta}, X^{s,delta}_vac in quantifiers.formal; X^{s,delta}_vac in genericity.ambient_space). J^-(q)') use whole-curve single-q non-containment, and quantifiers.ordered (56-62) binds no t0. visibility.definition (line 220) defines visibility with the tail ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)') and visibility.negation_conclusion (line 222) is the matching tail negation ('for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail ... is NOT contained'). Since whole-curve containment A(q) implies tail containment B(q,t0) and not conversely, 'not exists q A(q)' is STRICTLY WEAKER than 'not exists q exists t0 B(q,t0)'. quantifiers.negation (84-88) negates the tail predicate ('some ... geodesic ... is visible from I+'), so the formal block and its declared negation are not complements of each other.
